Thanks for the clear ask and for the CSV. Quick answers up front:
- We can provide a current subprocessor registry (attached).
- Redwood's standard notice window for new subprocessors is 30 days. The objection window we typically offer is 15 days from notice.

I appreciate that's shorter than what you proposed (60 / 30). Our rationale: many infra changes are operationally-driven and a shorter window lets us remediate without blocking critical patches. That said, we're willing to be flexible for contracted enterprise customers — happy to negotiate an extended notice on a per-deal basis.

Attached: DPA_Redline_Redwood_20250901.pdf (our redlines highlighting the notice/objection language). If you want, Neha (cc'd) can propose compromise language that balances your risk review needs with our operational cadence.

Subject: Re: Initial DPA questions — subprocessor list & objection timing

Jordan —

Thanks for the note and the CSV. We've discussed internally and propose the following compromise for the DPA: 45 days' notice prior to onboarding a new subprocessor; a 15-day customer objection window after notice; and a defined escalation path for high-risk objections. Key points: 

- Notice: Redwood will make commercially reasonable efforts to provide written notice 45 days before a material change that would introduce a new subprocessor that has access to customer data.
- Objection window: Customer has 15 calendar days from receipt of notice to submit a written objection with specific, reasonable basis tied to regulatory or contractual non-compliance.
- Escalation / mitigation: Upon objection, Redwood will (a) pause onboarding where technically feasible; (b) provide technical and compliance details within 5 business days; and (c) if parties cannot resolve within 10 business days, escalate to senior contacts with the option for short-term mitigations (e.g., data segmentation, temporary access restrictions) until a longer-term solution is agreed.
- Documentation & evidence: Redwood will provide a subprocessor risk pack (SOC/attestations, location, data access scope) upon request.

I am attaching a clean DPA that includes the above language and the current subprocessor registry. If Acme accepts, we will send the DocuSign envelope for signature.

DocuSign envelope: https://www.docusign.com/envelopes/ABC123DEF456
HubSpot record: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/67890

Please let us know by EOD Friday if this is acceptable, and we'll prepare the final signature packet.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
